title: Leak repairs, NPV against safety

blocks.text: This is the mock's whiteboard, coded. A gas utility's leak repairs each have a `cost`, an `npv` and the safety `risk` they remove, all in $k. Repairs that name the same `main` are alternatives for that main; a repair with `main=None` belongs to no group. The planners' question: **the most NPV within the budget, among the plans that remove at least `risk_floor` of risk**, with at most one repair per main.

`repairs.py` already creates one binary per repair. Write `add_epsilon_model(model, x, repairs, budget, risk_floor)`: the objective and every row. Write the formulation first (sets, parameters, variables with domains, objective with its sense, labelled rows), then code it.
The tests fix plans in and out and ask HiGHS whether the model accepts them, then solve the model and check the best plan, so any correct formulation passes. About ten lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Repair:
    rid: str
    cost: int            # $k
    npv: int             # $k
    risk: int            # safety risk removed, $k a year
    main: str | None = None   # repairs on the same main are alternatives


def select_variables(model: mathopt.Model, repairs: list[Repair]) -> dict[str, mathopt.Variable]:
    """Given: x[rid] = 1 when the repair is funded."""
    return {r.rid: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{r.rid}") for r in repairs}


def add_epsilon_model(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, repairs: list[Repair], budget: int, risk_floor: int) -> None:
    """The most NPV within the budget, among plans removing at least risk_floor, one repair per main."""
    # TODO: the objective and the rows of your formulation.
    return None


def build(repairs: list[Repair], budget: int, risk_floor: int) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="leak-repairs")
    x = select_variables(model, repairs)
    add_epsilon_model(model, x, repairs, budget, risk_floor)
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model, x = build([Repair("L1", 40, 30, 10), Repair("L2", 30, 25, 12)], 60, 10)
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
    print(result.termination.reason.name, {k: round(result.variable_values(v)) for k, v in x.items()})

a plan that removes too little risk is refused
two repairs on one main are refused
repairs that belong to no main may be funded together
the solve returns the plan with the most NPV among those above the floor
